paper.title: On Characterizations for Language Generation: Interplay of Hallucinations, Breadth, and Stability
paper.summary: Characterizes exact, approximate, exhaustive, unambiguous, and stable language generation; develops general uniqueness lower bounds, statistical consequences, and weaker notions of coverage. Lean proves incompatibility for several registered literal readings of stable fresh-support claims; mapping those readings back to the pinned source remains disputed pending named human correspondence review.

formalization_scope.summary: Lean covers the deterministic semantic equivalence for exact breadth, the semantic sufficiency direction for approximate breadth, and the Nat semantic stable-approximate equivalence. A cross-paper P04 bridge relates its exhaustive-generation interface to P05 weak Angluin but does not establish correspondence with the P05 source interface. Lean refutes registered literal readings of the stable exact-breadth and stable infinite-coverage claims and records a non-covering whole-target correction link; source correspondence for those readings still awaits named human confirmation. General lower-bound frameworks, effective realizations, statistical rates, and most Section 8 constructions remain unformalized.
specializations: The development models a support-valued generator as an arbitrary function on finite histories and does not claim Turing computability, sampling realizability, or support-oracle computability.
The stable approximate-breadth equivalence is formalized over Nat; no arbitrary-countable-universe transport theorem is provided.
The corrected stable exact result changes from literal unseen support to whole-target support after restoring observations and is not counted as coverage of the printed theorem.
gaps: The uniqueness and finite-non-uniqueness lower-bound frameworks of Theorems 3.5 and 3.10 are absent.
The necessity direction and effective realization of Theorem 3.8 are absent.
The P05 exhaustive-generation source interface has not been proved equivalent to the materially different P04 exhaustive interface used by the cross-paper bridge.
Unambiguous and stable unambiguous generation, stable exhaustive generation, and the statistical-rate theorems are outside the current formalization.
The source constructions for Proposition 8.4, Theorem 8.7's witness family, and Proposition 8.14 are not formalized.

Literal Definition 3.1 exact breadth and Definition 8.3 infinite coverage are incompatible with raw-support stability on complete infinite presentations; Lean refutes the registered literal readings rather than formalizing them, while source correspondence awaits named human confirmation.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Every theorem-, proposition-, and corollary-level result explicitly enumerated in the public P05 Paper Map correspondence table: Theorems 3.3, 3.5, 3.8, 3.10, 3.15, 4.3, 4.5, 5.2, and 5.3; Proposition 8.4; Theorem 8.7; Proposition 8.10 together with its mapped Corollary 8.11(2); and Proposition 8.14. The scope additionally includes Corollary 8.11(1), directly verified in the pinned arXiv v2 source as the other clause of that mapped corollary. Multi-clause characterization theorems are split into independently assessable claim cards.
exclusions: Definitions, lemmas, remarks, examples, proof-only intermediate results, and appendix discussion do not receive separate claim cards in this inventory.
Additional Figure 3 and Figure 4 table cells and Section 8 results not explicitly enumerated in the public P05 Paper Map remain outside this declared scope.

The source's footnote-level whole-target convention is not promoted to a separate source claim; the Lean whole-target theorem is recorded only as a non-covering correction link on the disputed literal-reading claim.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means complete for the Paper Map result scope plus the directly source-verified Corollary 8.11(1), not for every numbered object or informal assertion in arXiv v2. Corollary 8.11(1) was checked directly against arXiv:2412.18530v2; it has no named human correspondence audit. Source items sharing a mathematical conclusion, such as a Section 3 theorem and its Section 4 table extension, may appear as multiple source_refs on one claim card.

claims.title: Exact breadth is characterized by Angluin's condition
claims.statement_summary: For every countable collection of infinite languages, generation with exact breadth in the limit is possible if and only if the collection satisfies Angluin's condition; Theorem 4.3 repeats this as the exact-breadth component of its characterization table.

formalization.notes: The semantic set-valued equivalence is complete over an arbitrary countable universe. The Lean declarations do not certify the source's computable sampling, enumeration, and support-membership representation claims.

components.summary: Existence of an arbitrary support-valued exact-breadth generator is equivalent to Angluin's condition.
A succinct computable generator supports sampling, support enumeration, and support-membership decisions as described by the source.

lean_links.notes: Paper-facing wrapper restoring the source's standing infinite-language assumption.
Internal semantic equivalence used by the source-facing wrapper; it strengthens the registered source statement by dropping the standing infinite-language assumption.

relations.notes: Theorem 4.3 places exact breadth and unambiguous generation in the same Angluin-condition class.
Without stability, exact breadth requires full Angluin while approximate breadth requires only weak Angluin.

audit_refs.scope: Curated semantic correspondence; no named human source audit exists for P05.
Axiom-allowlist checks for the source-facing and internal semantic equivalences.

claims.title: Lower bound for unique generation properties
claims.statement_summary: Any generation property satisfying the paper's uniqueness criterion can be achieved on a countable language collection only if that collection satisfies Angluin's condition.

formalization.notes: The library proves particular Angluin characterizations but does not encode the source's generic uniqueness property or its diagonal lower bound.

relations.notes: Supplies the source's general necessity method for exact breadth.
Supplies the lower-bound method for unambiguous generation.

audit_refs.scope: Public P05 map records this theorem as unformalized; no named human source audit exists.

claims.title: Approximate breadth is characterized by weak Angluin
claims.statement_summary: For every countable collection of infinite languages, generation with approximate breadth in the limit is possible if and only if the collection satisfies the weak Angluin condition; Theorem 4.3 repeats the characterization in its breadth table.

formalization.notes: Lean proves the semantic weak-Angluin sufficiency construction. The finite-non-uniqueness necessity reduction and the source's effective implementation claims are absent.

components.summary: Weak Angluin's condition yields an arbitrary support-valued approximate-breadth generator.
Existence of an approximate-breadth generator implies weak Angluin's condition.
The sufficiency construction has the source's algorithmic sampling and membership-oracle realization.

lean_links.notes: Paper-facing wrapper for only the forward implication from weak Angluin to approximate breadth.
Internal semantic sufficiency theorem used by the source-facing wrapper.

relations.notes: Theorem 4.3 assigns both notions the weak Angluin characterization.
The necessity direction is obtained from the generic finite-non-uniqueness theorem in the source.

audit_refs.scope: Curated correspondence for the semantic sufficiency direction and documented omission of necessity.
Axiom-allowlist checks for the source-facing and internal semantic sufficiency theorems.

claims.title: Lower bound for finitely non-unique generation properties

formalization.notes: Neither the abstract finite-non-uniqueness predicate nor its diagonal lower bound is present in Lean.

relations.notes: Provides the paper's necessity method for approximate breadth.
Provides the paper's necessity method for exhaustive generation.

formalization.notes: P05 has no native unambiguous-generation predicate or source theorem wrapper; related P03 results use a different interface.

claims.title: Exhaustive generation is characterized by weak Angluin
claims.statement_summary: For every countable collection of infinite languages, exhaustive generation in the limit is possible if and only if the collection satisfies the weak Angluin condition.

The repository does not prove that P04's output interface is faithfully equivalent to the P05 source notion, so the bridge is related evidence and contributes no coverage to this claim.

claims.title: Stable approximate breadth is characterized by Angluin's condition
claims.statement_summary: For a countable collection of infinite languages, a raw-support-stable approximate-breadth generator exists if and only if the collection satisfies Angluin's condition; Theorem 4.5 repeats this clause in the stable breadth table.

source_assessment.notes: Approximate breadth permits observed target elements in the support and is coherent with raw-support stability.

formalization.notes: The complete semantic equivalence is proved for Nat. The source's arbitrary countable string universe and effective generator realization are not formalized.

components.summary: Over Nat, existence of a stable approximate-breadth support function is equivalent to Angluin's condition.
Transport the stable approximate equivalence from Nat to the source's arbitrary countable string universe.
The stable approximate generator has the source's computable sampling and support-query realization.

lean_links.notes: Paper-facing Nat semantic equivalence with the source's infinite-language assumption restored.
Internal theorem combining P05 sufficiency with the P03 semantic necessity reduction.

relations.notes: Adding raw-support stability raises the structural condition from weak Angluin to full Angluin.
Theorem 4.5 places all stable breadth notions in the Angluin-condition class.
Theorem 4.5 places all stable breadth notions in the Angluin-condition class.

claims.title: Literal stable exact-breadth characterization
claims.statement_summary: Under the literal combination of Definition 3.1, which requires support equal to the unseen target K minus the current sample, and Definition 3.14, which requires raw support to become constant, Theorems 3.15 and 4.5 claim stable exact breadth is equivalent to Angluin's condition.

source_refs.locator: Theorem 4.5, stable exact-breadth bullet and footnote 3
source_refs.notes: Footnote 3 switches to a sample-allowing convention without changing the earlier literal definition.

source_assessment.notes: Lean refutes the registered literal reading: on a complete presentation of an infinite target, literal exact breadth removes each newly observed element while raw stability requires support to remain fixed. The source's footnote-level whole-target convention supports a coherent correction but is not the literal printed statement. Source correspondence for the literal reading awaits named human confirmation.

formalization.notes: The countertheorems and corrected whole-target theorems are deliberately non-covering links. The corrected theorem must not be counted as a formalization of the disputed literal-reading claim.

lean_links.notes: Paper-facing contradiction under the source's standing infinite-language assumption.
Separate whole-target/sample-restored repair. Its corrected relationship intentionally contributes no coverage to the literal theorem.
Internal corrected theorem; it is not the literal Theorem 3.15.

relations.notes: The inconsistency appears only after literal unseen-support exact breadth is combined with raw stability.

claims.title: Statistical rates for exact breadth
claims.statement_summary: No nontrivial language collection admits an exact-breadth rate faster than exp(-n); identifiable collections achieve exp(-n), while non-identifiable collections admit no exact-breadth rate.

formalization.notes: The P05 development is deterministic and contains no distributions, expected error, universal rates, or exponential bounds.

relations.notes: The no-rate conclusion uses the identification/exact-breadth boundary.

audit_refs.scope: Public P05 map explicitly excludes statistical rate statements.

claims.title: Statistical rates for approximate breadth
claims.statement_summary: No nontrivial language collection admits an approximate-breadth rate faster than exp(-n), while weak-Angluin collections achieve exp(-n); the printed final clause states that collections failing weak Angluin admit no exact-breadth rate.

source_refs.notes: The final sentence omits the verb 'satisfy' and says exact breadth although the theorem is about approximate breadth.

source_assessment.notes: The first two clauses are clear. The literal final clause is logically compatible with the earlier exact-breadth theorem, but its grammar and use of 'exact' in an approximate-breadth theorem suggest a possible source typo; this registry does not silently rewrite it.

formalization.notes: No statistical rate component is formalized.

relations.notes: The achievable-rate boundary uses weak Angluin.

audit_refs.scope: Public P05 map excludes statistical rates; the possible typo remains unaudited.

claims.title: Every countable family admits infinite coverage
claims.statement_summary: A modification of the Kleinberg-Mullainathan generator achieves literal infinite coverage in the limit for every countable language collection by outputting an infinite valid support disjoint from the observed sample.

source_assessment.notes: The proposed support explicitly removes the current sample and need not stabilize.

formalization.notes: Lean defines the literal infinite-coverage predicate but does not implement or prove the Proposition 8.4 modification.

relations.notes: Infinite coverage is universal without stability but fails for some collections once raw-support stability is imposed.

audit_refs.scope: Public P05 map records the source construction as unformalized.

claims.title: Weak Angluin does not suffice for stable infinite coverage
claims.statement_summary: There exists a countable language collection satisfying weak Angluin for which no raw-support-stable generator achieves literal infinite coverage.

source_assessment.notes: The literal theorem is true, but Lean proves the negative stable-infinite-coverage component for every infinite-language family, revealing that the separation follows from the same raw-stability/unseen-support convention conflict rather than the source's special witness geometry.

formalization.notes: Lean proves a stronger universal literal incompatibility but does not formalize the source's concrete weak-Angluin witness family and its full existential package.

components.summary: No stable generator can have literal infinite coverage on a complete presentation of an infinite target.
Construct the source's countable family, prove weak Angluin, and package it with the stable-coverage impossibility.

lean_links.notes: Stronger than the theorem's negative component because it applies to every indexed family of infinite languages, not only the source witness.

relations.notes: Shows that adding raw-support stability destroys the universal existence result.

audit_refs.scope: Curated qualification distinguishing the missing source witness from Lean's stronger literal incompatibility theorem.
Axiom-allowlist check for the universal stable infinite-coverage impossibility theorem.

claims.title: Finite closure dimension yields stable infinite coverage
claims.statement_summary: For a language collection of finite closure dimension, a stable generator using a version-space-intersection membership oracle and the dimension value achieves literal infinite coverage after d(L)+1 distinct target examples.

source_assessment.notes: Lean refutes the registered literal reading: the proof stabilizes to a nonempty support containing target elements, while literal Definition 8.3 requires support to remain disjoint from every growing complete sample. The incompatibility is independent of closure dimension and oracle access, but source correspondence for this reading awaits named human confirmation.

formalization.notes: The registered Lean declarations refute the literal reading rather than formalize the disputed source claim.

audit_refs.scope: Codex-assisted source finding explicitly awaiting named human confirmation.
Axiom-allowlist checks for the paper-facing and internal countertheorems.

claims.title: Finite families admit literal stable exact breadth
claims.statement_summary: Every finite collection of infinite languages admits a raw-support-stable generator with literal exact breadth using only membership-oracle access.

source_assessment.notes: Lean refutes the registered literal reading: finite families still contain infinite target languages, and literal support K minus the growing sample cannot become raw-constant on a complete presentation. Corollary 8.11(1) was directly checked in arXiv v2, but its source correspondence to this reading awaits named human confirmation.

formalization.notes: The countertheorem and whole-target correction are non-covering links; the corrected result is not counted as the literal corollary.

lean_links.notes: The universal family-level obstruction applies in particular to finite collections encoded as indexed families.

The whole-target/sample-restored theorem supplies a generic corrected equivalence. Applying it to this finite-family corollary additionally requires a finite-family ConditionTwo fact not linked by this card, and it intentionally contributes no coverage to the literal corollary.

relations.notes: Finite collections are a special case of the disputed literal stable-exact reading.

audit_refs.scope: The public map documents the exact-stability convention conflict. Corollary 8.11(1) was checked directly in the pinned arXiv v2 source as the finite-family clause but has no named human correspondence audit.
Axiom-allowlist checks for the exact-stability obstruction and whole-target correction.

claims.title: Finite families admit bounded-sample stable infinite coverage
claims.statement_summary: Every finite language collection admits a raw-support-stable generator with literal infinite coverage after d(L)+1 distinct examples, using only membership-oracle access.

source_assessment.notes: Lean refutes the registered literal reading: an infinite-coverage support that remains disjoint from a complete growing sample cannot be a nonempty raw-stable set. The conflict is independent of finiteness, closure dimension, and oracle access, but source correspondence for this reading awaits named human confirmation.

formalization.notes: Lean refutes the registered literal reading rather than formalizing the disputed source claim.

lean_links.notes: Paper-facing countertheorem explicitly covers Proposition 8.10 and Corollary 8.11(2).

relations.notes: The source derives the finite-family clause from Proposition 8.10 and finite closure dimension.

claims.title: Strictly increasing infinite coverage below weak Angluin
claims.statement_summary: There exists a countable language collection failing weak Angluin that nevertheless admits a generator with infinite coverage and strictly increasing coverage in the limit.

source_refs.notes: Footnote 17 switches to a sample-allowing version of infinite coverage for the subsequent discussion.

source_assessment.notes: The proposition cites literal Definition 8.3, but its proof and footnote 17 use an alternate convention allowing observed samples in the support. The intended separation may be valid under that convention; its relationship to the literal unseen-support definition has not been audited.

formalization.notes: Lean has neither the strictly increasing coverage predicate nor the arithmetic-progression witness and does not resolve the convention switch.

relations.notes: Strengthens coverage dynamics on a particular family while dropping weak Angluin.

audit_refs.scope: Public map records Proposition 8.14 as unformalized; the footnote-level convention switch lacks named human review.
